candidate.title: FAIRE-Seq/Sono-Seq
candidate.scope: Grouped Illumina FAIRE-Seq/Sono-Seq explanatory schematic, interpreted at its depicted chromatin-to-purified-DNA boundary. The far-left yellow-highlighted chromatin vignette names the targets; it is not a separate workflow or transformation. One unbranched arrow route shows open DNA within chromatin, formalin crosslinking, sonication, and phenol extraction with aqueous-phase DNA purification. The primary papers resolve common fixation/sonication but distinct recovery mechanisms: the drawn direct aqueous-selection route describes FAIRE; Sono-Seq requires reversal of crosslinks before extraction and size selection. Those unshown Sono-Seq distinctions are recorded in applicability and correction, not silently inserted into the drawing. Library construction and sequencing are downstream interfaces supported by text, not depicted operations. No claim of identical complete implementations or historical priority is made.

operations.label: Crosslink protein and DNA with formalin
operations.description: Act on chromatin containing exposed and nucleosome-associated DNA to produce protein–DNA crosslinked chromatin. Crosslink marks appear on the nucleosome icons; the exposed DNA interval remains drawn.
operations.mechanism: Formaldehyde-mediated fixation links chromatin proteins to DNA. FAIRE exploits differences in crosslinking: histones are readily crosslinked, whereas nucleosome-depleted regions are less efficiently crosslinked to protein.
operations.information_effect: Chromatin protein association is encoded in differential crosslink retention. This is not protein-specific capture and does not identify the bound regulatory factor.

operations.label: Phenol extract and purify DNA from the aqueous phase
operations.description: On the drawn direct route, extract the sonicated, still-crosslinked material and purify aqueous-phase DNA. The retained output is a DNA preparation enriched for nucleosome-depleted genomic regions by FAIRE.
operations.mechanism: For FAIRE, DNA covalently crosslinked to protein is preferentially retained at the aqueous/organic interphase; DNA without these crosslinks preferentially enters the aqueous phase and is recovered. The interphase is a nonretained fate explained by the paper, not an additional retained branch drawn here.
operations.information_effect: The readout carrier is recovered genomic DNA. Downstream library sequencing maps the recovered sequences to genomic loci and estimates regional enrichment for accessible/nucleosome-depleted chromatin. Recovery is a biochemical enrichment, not a guarantee of regulatory function or exact protein occupancy. It does not reveal the identity of bound regulatory proteins. This local extraction instance, with still-crosslinked input, is not assigned to Sono-Seq.

method_scopes.rationale: FAIRE-Seq means FAIRE enrichment coupled to DNA sequencing. All three local operations apply to the FAIRE preparation drawn here: fixation, sonication, and phenol partition of still-crosslinked chromatin with aqueous-phase DNA recovery. The recovered genomic DNA becomes a sequencing library outside the drawn boundary, and mapped sequences report enriched nucleosome-depleted loci. FAIRE-qPCR and FAIRE-chip are alternative detection interfaces described in the papers, not targets or branches of this assigned image. The 2006 reference uses the FAIRE isolation component with microarrays; the 2009 and 2012 protocols explicitly describe sequencing. No particular listed commercial library kit is specified by the drawing.

method_scopes.rationale: Sono-Seq is a distinct grouped target, not an alias for FAIRE-Seq. The primary paper explicitly supports the depicted fixation and sonication of fixed chromatin, so these local operations apply. It reverses protein–DNA crosslinks before phenol/chloroform extraction, retains DNA that had been crosslinked, and size-selects fragments for sequencing. Those steps are absent from this diagram. Therefore o_recover, whose fixed input s_sheared has not undergone reversal, and its FAIRE-selected output s_dna are not Sono-Seq recovery instances. Phenol extraction in the paper shares a purification purpose but has a different input history and selection effect. The downstream Sono-Seq library represents selected sonication products; mapped fragment-end enrichment reports sonication-sensitive chromatin, often near active promoters. The paper finds patterns distinct from FAIRE, so neither identical nucleosome-free selection nor interchangeability is supported. Applicability is resolved at the schematic/component scope; the complete Sono-Seq workflow is not drawn.
